questions.prompt: Why is `status = 200` used on the gateway redirect instead of `301` or `302`?
questions.explanation: A 200 is a rewrite: the server proxies to the internal function without changing the visible URL, keeping the internal path hidden and the public contract stable.
options: It is a server-side rewrite/proxy that hides the internal path while the browser still sees the public URL
It tells the browser to cache the page forever
It is required for any redirect to work at all

questions.prompt: Redirect rules are evaluated top to bottom with first-match-wins. What follows from this?
questions.explanation: Because the first match wins, a broad `/agronomy-api/*` placed before `/agronomy-api/health` would intercept the health requests; specific rules go first.
options: Order does not matter as long as all rules exist
Specific rules must come before broad wildcards or the wildcard will swallow them
Wildcards should always be listed first
Each rule must have a unique status code

questions.prompt: Routing in `netlify.toml` lets you repoint a public path to a renamed or relocated function without changing the frontend.
questions.explanation: True. The client only knows the public path; changing the redirect target is a config change invisible to the frontend.
